value.rationale: A sharp, naturally defined finite-population extinction-risk phenomenon shows that three ecologically meaningful indicators may be pairwise independent although the entire guild can never disappear. N=9 is the exact first feasible pollinator census when two survive and all individual extinction events remain nondegenerate; exactly three incidence types and a unique no-unused-partner network are classified. N=10 is impossible, showing the threshold is not a generic monotone sampling-size fact. This warns against replacing higher-order coextinction risks with pairwise models. It is a structural finite classification, not a routine marginal probability calculation.
